representations.text: During March 30–April 12, RMSSD briefly fell against a stable 28-day baseline of 44.5 ms (43–47): four consecutive days, April 3–6, measured 22–28 ms, followed by return to 43–47 throughout April 7–12. This lowered the window mean to 39.4 ms (−11.6%); it was not a sustained decline. Resting heart rate stayed at 55–57 bpm, averaging 56.0 versus 56.1 baseline, including during the RMSSD dip. Sleep averaged 468.5 versus 470.5 minutes, with starts at 22:42–22:58 and waking consistently at 07:00; weekday/weekend sleep was similar. Steps remained near 8,061 versus 8,054 daily. Moving minutes decreased modestly, 55.4 to 53.0, especially weekends (50.8 versus 55.6). Low movement stayed near 450 versus 448 minutes, in ten daytime bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Activity beginning at 21:00 had only a weak association with following-wake-date sleep (r=−0.25, 13 pairs). No metrics were missing.

Steps dropped abruptly from the 28-day baseline mean of 8,009/day to 2,335 during March 30–April 12 (−5,675; −70.8%). Every window day remained at 2,064–2,636, below the baseline range of 7,607–8,342, with no return. Both weekdays and weekends were lower (2,278 and 2,477/day). This change did not coincide with comparable changes in moving minutes (54.6 versus 55.1) or low movement (452.6 versus 451.4 minutes). Weekend moving minutes fell to 52.3 from 56.9, while weekdays averaged 55.5 versus 54.5. Activity remained one continuous bout beginning at 21:00; daytime low movement comprised ten bouts with five-minute gaps. Sleep was stable at 469.6 versus 469.8 minutes, starting near 22:50 and ending at 07:00, without a substantial weekday/weekend difference. Resting heart rate and RMSSD remained near baseline: 56.0 versus 55.7 bpm and 45.3 versus 45.1 ms. Activity versus following-wake-date sleep showed a modest negative association (r=−0.36, 13 pairs), without establishing causation. Coverage was complete.

March 30–April 12 contained two distinct, nonoverlapping four-day changes. Resting heart rate rose to 65–67 bpm on April 3–6 against the 28-day baseline mean of 56.0 (55–57), then returned to 55–57 for April 7–12. RMSSD stayed at 44–47 ms during that rise, then fell to 23–26 on April 7–10 against baseline 45.0 (43–47), returning to 45 on April 11–12. Window means were 58.7 bpm and 38.9 ms; these averages obscure the separate episodes. The heart-rate rise crossed Friday–Monday; the RMSSD dip occurred Tuesday–Friday, rather than a repeating weekend pattern. Other measures remained close to baseline: sleep 470.4 versus 469.8 minutes, steps 7,996 versus 8,043, moving minutes 55.3 versus 54.9, and low movement 446.6 versus 450.7 minutes. Sleep starts remained near 22:50 with 07:00 waking. Continuous activity began at 21:00; low movement had five-minute interruptions between ten bouts. Activity and following-wake-date sleep had little association (r=0.10). No metrics were missing.

Across March 30–April 12, steps averaged 6,433 on 13 observed days versus the 28-day baseline of 9,552 (−3,119; −32.6%). All observed values, 6,262–6,675, were below baseline’s 9,307–9,793, with no observed return. The reduction affected weekdays and weekends (6,404 and 6,500 versus 9,517 and 9,640). April 7 had only 360 daytime wear minutes, so steps, moving minutes and low movement are missing; continuity across that date is uncertain. Moving minutes changed modestly, 53.5 versus 55.1, and low movement averaged 450.6 versus 447.8 minutes. Activity remained a continuous bout starting at 21:00; low movement comprised ten daytime bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Steps and moving minutes were essentially unrelated within the window (r=0.006). Sleep and nighttime estimates were complete and stable: sleep 469.9 versus 469.5 minutes, starts near 22:50 and 07:00 waking; resting heart rate 56.3 versus 56.1 bpm; RMSSD 45.5 versus 45.2 ms. Activity versus following-wake-date sleep showed only a modest negative association (r=−0.32, 12 pairs).
